title: The psychophysics of affect in large language models
abstract: arXiv:2610.40985v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Good decisions often require considering how outcomes will feel. Yet large language models (LLMs) increasingly enter decision workflows, despite little being known about how they map outcomes to feelings or use those mappings in choice. We tested how LLMs anticipated gambling or stock-trading outcomes would feel and whether they incorporated these ratings into choice. When outcomes were rated in isolation, ratings exhibited diminishing sensitivity to magnitude, resembling human value functions; but models rated gains more intensely than equivalent losses, an inversion of canonical loss aversion we call silicon gain amplification. When outcomes were rated together, enabling direct comparison, ratings linearised. In choice, the gain-loss asymmetry largely disappeared, and models' own ratings did not reliably explain their choices better than monetary utility did. translated_title: 大语言模型中情感的心理物理学
translated_abstract: 良好的决策往往需要考虑结果将会带来的感受。然而，大语言模型（LLM）正日益进入决策工作流程，但人们对它们如何将结果映射为感受、以及如何在选择中使用这些映射却知之甚少。我们测试了大语言模型如何预期赌博或股票交易结果带来的感受，以及它们是否将这些评分纳入选择决策。当结果被单独评分时，评分对量级表现出递减的敏感性，与人类的价值函数相似；但模型对收益的评分比对等额损失的评分更为强烈，这是对经典损失厌恶的一种反转，我们称之为“硅基收益放大”。当结果被一起评分、可以进行直接比较时，评分趋于线性化。在选择题任务中，收益与损失之间的不对称性基本消失，且模型自身的评分在解释其选择方面并不比货币效用更可靠。这些发现揭示了从结果到情感的可塑映射，并引发了相关问题……
tldr: 本研究首次系统测量了大语言模型将结果映射为情感的心理物理规律，发现模型对收益的情感反应强于等额损失（与人类损失厌恶相反的“硅基收益放大”现象），且这种结果到情感的映射会随评分情境和决策任务而显著改变，具有高度可塑性。
en_tdlr: This study reveals that LLMs exhibit "silicon gain amplification"—rating gains more intensely than equivalent losses, the inverse of human loss aversion—and that their outcome-to-affect mappings are malleable, linearizing under direct comparison and largely disappearing in choice.
